methods: Design: cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic. Population: Age >=18 years (analytic n = 6,847). Outcome: Thrombocytopenia - platelets <150 x10^9/L. Exposure: Liver stiffness (VCTE median). Comparator: per-unit contrast along the exposure (lower vs higher values); quartiles as sensitivity. Covariates: Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, Body mass index, Diabetes (self-report, medication, or HbA1c >=6.5%), Smoking status. Descriptive: survey-weighted Table 1 by thrombocytopenia - platelets <150 x10^9/l; weighted prevalence with 95% CIs. Model: prevalence ratios (survey-weighted Poisson regression); sequential models: Unadjusted, Adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity, Fully adjusted (primary). Effect modification: interaction tests and stratified estimates by sex, age group. Survey design: Taylor linearisation with strata and PSUs; weight WTMECPRP; design df = 25. Sensitivity analyses: 6 prespecified. Missing data: complete-case primary analysis; multiple imputation as sensitivity. Reporting: STROBE; plan pre-registered by hash before data access.

limitations.text: Cross-sectional: exposure and outcome are measured at the same visit, so the direction of association cannot be established.
Residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded in an observational analysis.
E-value 1.68: a modest unmeasured confounder (RR ≈ 1.7 with both exposure and outcome) could explain the association.
Complete-case loss: 14.2% of the analytic sample (1131) lack >=1 covariate. Multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis recommended.
Raw values within plausible ranges: Out-of-range values: BMXBMI (0 low, 1 high); LBXGH (1 low, 0 high); LBXPLTSI (0 low, 1 high)

certainty.meaning: The true association is probably close to the estimate, but may be substantially different.

domains.reason: Cross-sectional design already reflected in the Low starting level; adjusted, pre-specified analysis with design audit passed.
Direction and inference stable across 4 sensitivity analyses.
US civilian non-institutionalised population; outcome measured directly.
95% CI 1.16-1.23 excludes no effect and is reasonably narrow.
Cannot be judged from a single study; pre-registration by plan hash reduces selective reporting.

rating_up.reason: Gradient across exposure quartiles (P for trend .004).

certainty.caveat: GRADE rates bodies of evidence; this single-study rating summarises how much this analysis can contribute and should be re-rated in any systematic review.

assumptions: Outcome prevalence assumed 10% (run the blinded probe for the real rate band).
Design effect 1.8 (typical for NHANES; the post-run check uses the actual design-based SE).
